name: Gold Fusion
lede: Gold Fusion is a dull, yellowish brown rather than a metallic gold, and one of the most common colors in our entire painting archive.

sections.title: A compound name, no earlier record
sections.body: Gold Fusion pairs "gold" with "fusion"; Wikipedia's color list is our only source for the name, with no further origin documented [1]. The hex value, #85754E, reads as a dull, yellowish brown on screen rather than a metallic gold [1]. Its nearest named look-alikes in our library are [[buffy-olive]], [[green-brown]], [[grey-brown]] and [[hair-brown]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this brown in 18.69 percent of the 23,781 paintings we have, 4,445 of them, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 2,527 [2]. That makes it more common than 97 percent of the named colors in our archive [2]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 39 percent of the 2,527 paintings where it appears, measured by lightness rank within each painting so varnish cannot fake it [2]. Pieter Claesz is its most devoted painter, using it in 7 of 13 works here, 3.7 times the baseline rate of the museums those works come from [2]. It shares canvases with Japanese Bush Warbler and Ecru-Olive more than chance alone would predict [2]. The archive's first match for this hue is dated 900, in a painting attributed to Zhao Guangfu, though our early centuries are thin, so this is a floor on presence, not a claim about when the name began [2].

origin.first_recorded: undocumented in the sources we hold
